# categorical predictors

## lines again..  


::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
**The general idea:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{outcome}} &= \color{blue}{\text{model}} +  \color{black}{\text{error}} \\
\end{align}
$$
**The linear model:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{y} &= \color{blue}{\underset{\underset{\text{intercept}}{\uparrow}}{b_0} + \underset{\underset{\text{slope}}{\uparrow}}{b_1} \cdot x} + \color{black}{\epsilon}
\end{align}
$$

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
set.seed(65683728)
df <- tibble(
  x = runif(100,0,10),
  y = rnorm(100,33+2*x,3)
)

fitw = lm(y~x,df)
segsw <- tibble(x1 = 0:6, x2 = x1+1) |> 
  mutate(
    y1 = map_dbl(x1,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    y2 = map_dbl(x2,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    xlp = (x1+x2)/2,
    ylp = (y1+y2)/2
  )
df |> 
  ggplot(aes(x,y))+
  geom_point(size=3,alpha=.4)+
  stat_smooth(method=lm,se=FALSE,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(x=0,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x2,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y2),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF") +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:10)
```
:::
::::

## that example again..  


::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%" style="font-size:.5em"}

**The idea:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{outcome}} &= \color{blue}{\text{model}} + \color{black}{\text{error}} \\
\quad \\
\color{red}{y} &= \color{blue}{\underset{\underset{\text{intercept}}{\uparrow}}{b_0} + \underset{\underset{\text{slope}}{\uparrow}}{b_1} \cdot x} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
\end{align}
$$

**Our model:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolving_Score}} &= \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{Nights_Disrupted}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon} \\
\end{align}
$$

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
**Our estimated model:**  
$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolving_Score}} &= \,\,\,\color{blue}{58 \,\,\,- 1.5 \cdot \text{Nights_Disrupted}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
\end{align}
$$
:::

:::
:::{.column width="50%"}

:::{.r-stack}

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
set.seed(65683728)
sleepdf <- tibble(
  n_disrupted = rep(0:7,e=10),
  psolve = (58 - 1.5 * n_disrupted) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(80,0,7) ~ rep(0:7,e=10)))
) |> slice_sample(prop=1)


fitw = lm(psolve~n_disrupted,sleepdf)

segsw <- tibble(x1 = 0:6, x2 = x1+1) |> 
  mutate(
    y1 = map_dbl(x1,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    y2 = map_dbl(x2,~(c(1,.)%*%coef(fitw))[1]),
    xlp = (x1+x2)/2,
    ylp = (y1+y2)/2
  )
sleepdf |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=n_disrupted,y=psolve))+
  geom_point(size=3,col="tomato1",alpha=.5)+
  stat_smooth(method=lm,se=FALSE,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(x=0,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x2,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y2),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF") +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:7)
```

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 8
sleepdf |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=n_disrupted,y=psolve))+
  geom_point(size=3,col="tomato1",alpha=.5)+
  stat_smooth(method=lm,se=FALSE,color="#0000FF",lwd=1) +
  geom_point(x=0,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x1,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y1),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(data = segsw, aes(x=x2,xend=x2,y=y1,yend=y2),
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF") +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=0:7)+
  annotate(geom="label",label="58",x=.5,y=65,hjust=0,col="blue",size=5) +
  geom_curve(aes(x=0.5, xend=0, y=65, yend=58.5), 
             col="blue", size=0.5, curvature = 0.2, 
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.03, "npc"))) +
  annotate(geom="label",label="-1.5",x=1.5,y=60,hjust=0,col="blue",size=5) +
  geom_curve(aes(x=1.5, xend=1, y=60, yend=57), 
             col="blue", size=0.5, curvature = 0, 
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.02, "npc")))+
  annotate(geom="label",label="-1.5",x=2.5,y=58,hjust=0,col="blue",size=5) +
  geom_curve(aes(x=2.5, xend=2, y=58, yend=55.5), 
             col="blue", size=0.2, curvature = 0, 
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.02, "npc")))+
  annotate(geom="label",label="-1.5",x=3.5,y=56,hjust=0,col="blue",size=5) +
  geom_curve(aes(x=3.5, xend=3, y=56, yend=54), alpha=.2,
             col="blue", size=0.1, curvature = 0, 
             arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.02, "npc")))
```

## that example again.. (2) {.smaller}

**Design:**  
People have 0, 1, 2, .... nights of sleep disruption.  

**Data:**  
```{r}
head(sleepdf)
```

**Model:**  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{NightsDisrupted}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}

**Predictions:**  

$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 0} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 1} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 2} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot 3} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
...

:::

## example 2 {.smaller}

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(65683728)
xbin = sample(c("Good","Bad"),60,T,prob=c(.6,.4))
sleepdf2 <- tibble(
  sleep_quality = xbin,
  psolve = (50 + 7.5 * (sleep_quality=="Good")) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(60,0,7) ~ xbin))
) |> slice_sample(prop=1)

```


**Design:**  
People have "good" or "bad" sleep

**Data:**  
```{r}
head(sleepdf2)
```

**Model:**  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{SleepQuality}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}

**Predictions:**  

$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{'Bad'}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \,\,\,\color{blue}{b_0 \,\,\,+ b_1 \cdot \text{'Good'}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  

:::

## doing maths with words  

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="50%"}
```{r}
#| echo: false
head(sleepdf2)
```

- We can't multiply a number by a word.  
    - $\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{'Bad'}}$ and $\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{'Good'}}$ don't make sense 
    
:::
:::{.column width="50%" .fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: false
sleepdf2 |> 
  mutate(
    isGood = (sleep_quality=="Good")*1, .after=sleep_quality
  ) |> head()
```

- But we can represent categories as binary 0/1 variables:  
- And using the binary variable makes the maths work:  
    - $\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 0}$ and $\color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 1}$ are both arithmetically valid

:::
:::: 


## expressing categories as numbers

With just two levels, we just map 0s and 1s to the two categories:  

```{r}
sleepdf2 |> 
  mutate(
    isGood = ifelse(sleep_quality=="Good", 1, 0)
  )
```

## with 3+, we need more
#### (this doesn't come up again until DAPR2) 

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(3588)
xbin = sample(c("Good","Average","Bad"),60,T,prob=c(.2,.6,.2))
sleepdf3 <- tibble(
  sleep_quality = xbin,
  psolve = (50 + 7.5 * (sleep_quality=="Good")) + 
    residuals(lm(rnorm(60,0,7) ~ xbin))
) |> slice_sample(prop=1)

```

```{r}
sleepdf3 |> 
  mutate(
    isGood = ifelse(sleep_quality=="Good", 1, 0),
    isBad = ifelse(sleep_quality=="Bad",1,0)
  )
```


## lm() does it for us!  

- variables in R can be:  
    - numeric
    - factor
    - character
    
- when a predictor is either character or factor, `lm()` will do this all for us.  


## lm() does it for us! - example 2

```{r}
head(sleepdf2)

sleepqual_mod <- lm(psolve ~ sleep_quality, data = sleepdf2)

sleepqual_mod
```

the category named in the coefficients is the one that is coded as 1.  
the category not mentioned is coded as 0.  

## what are $b_0$ and $b_1$?  

**The Model:**  
$$
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(SleepQuality="Good")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
$$

- for people with "Bad" sleep quality:  

$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} &= \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 0} \\
 &= \color{blue}{b_0} \\
\end{align}
$$  

- for people with "Good" sleep quality:  

$$
\begin{align}
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} &= \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot 1} \\
 &= \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 }
\end{align}
$$  


## what are $b_0$ and $b_1$?  

**The Model:**  
$$
\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(SleepQuality="Good")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}
$$

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| code-fold: true
sleepdf2 |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=sleep_quality, y=psolve))+
  # jitter adds a little noise to the data, so that points don't overlap
  # height and width control how much noise 
  geom_jitter(size = 3, alpha = .5, height = 0, width = .1) +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)
```

:::{.r-stack}

```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(3455)
sleepdf2 |> 
  ggplot(aes(x=sleep_quality, y=psolve))+
  geom_jitter(size = 3, alpha = .5, height = 0, width = .1) +
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)+
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c(" \nBad"," \nGood"))
```

:::{.fragment fragment-index=1}
```{r}
#| echo: false
set.seed(3455)
sleepdf2 |>

  geom_jitter(size = 3, alpha = .5, height = 0, width = .1) +
  scale_x_discrete(labels = c("0\nBad","1\nGood"))+
  theme_quarto(title_font_size = 28)
```

:::

:::{.fragment fragment-index=2}

fitw = sleepqual_mod
set.seed(3455)

  geom_point(x=1,y=coef(fitw)[1],col="#0000FF",size=5)+
  geom_segment(x=1,xend=2,y=coef(fitw)[1],yend=coef(fitw)[1],
               lty="dashed",col="#0000FF")+
  geom_segment(x=2,xend=2,y=coef(fitw)[1],yend=sum(coef(fitw)),

## changing reference category?  

Do we want:  
<br>
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(SleepQuality="Good")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$  
  
  <br>
or  
  <br>
$\color{red}{\text{ProblemSolvingScore}} = \color{blue}{b_0 + b_1 \cdot \text{(SleepQuality="Bad")}} + \color{black}{\varepsilon}$

## R defaults to alphabetical

::::{.columns}
:::{.column width="65%"}

```{r}
#| eval: false
summary(sleepqual_mod)
```
```{r}
#| echo: false
.pp(summary(sleepqual_mod),l = list(c(1:14),0,0,0,0))
```

:::
:::{.column style="width:35%;font-size:.7em;color:#cc3363"}

<br><br><br><br><br><br><br><br>

- "Good" is mentioned here to indicate moving from the reference category to "Good"  
- the intercept (the reference category) must therefore be "Bad" because it's not mentioned in the slope  


:::
::::

## factors give us control

```{r}
#| eval: false
sleepdf2 <- sleepdf2 |>
  mutate(
                                                # note the ordering
    sleep_quality = factor(sleep_quality, levels = c("Good", "Bad"))
    
  )

sleepqual_mod <- lm(psolve ~ sleep_quality, data = sleepdf2)
sleepqual_mod
```

:::{.fragment}
```{r}
#| echo: false
sleepdf2 <- sleepdf2 |>
  mutate(
    sleep_quality = factor(sleep_quality, 
                           levels = c("Good", "Bad"))
  )

sleepqual_mod <- lm(psolve ~ sleep_quality, data = sleepdf2)
sleepqual_mod
```
:::

## Block 4 skills involved in this week's lecture and/or workshop

- **A10** I can represent binary predictors using treatment coding.
- **A7** I can use a fitted simple linear model to predict an outcome value for a given predictor value
- **A8** I can appropriately interpret the parameters of a simple linear model.
- **C3** I can describe in writing the results of a given simple linear model.
- **I8** I can identify the null hypothesis being tested for the parameters of a linear model.
